sections.h2: Where is Mansfield, CT, and how is the town laid out?
sections.html:
Mansfield is a town in Tolland County, Connecticut, and it counts 25,892 residents in the 2020 census. It covers 45.5 square miles, most of it land, and it sits in the Capitol Planning Region.

The town is spread across many small settlements rather than one center. Wikipedia lists Atwoodville, Eagleville, Gurleyville, Mansfield Center, Mansfield Depot, Mansfield Hollow, Mount Hope, Spring Hill and Storrs, among others. Storrs is the largest and is anchored by the main campus of the University of Connecticut. Mansfield Center is the other major village and borders Willimantic to the south.

Part of the town is also described as belonging to Connecticut's Quiet Corner, the more rural northeast of the state. That mix of campus village, older hamlets and farmland means two Mansfield houses can sit in very different settings and draw very different buyers.

  • Storrs: campus-adjacent, with the mixed-use downtown built in the mid-2000s.
  • Mansfield Center: mostly a bedroom community with a small business district.
  • Gurleyville, Mansfield Hollow and Atwoodville: older village areas with historic districts.

sections.h2: What is the history of Mansfield?
sections.html:
Mansfield was incorporated in October 1702 after separating from Windham. It was first part of Windham County and moved to Tolland County in 1827, after a town meeting in 1826 voted to ask the General Assembly for the change.

The town has some unusual industrial history. The first silk mill in the United States was built here, and Mansfield and nearby Willimantic were important to thread and textile manufacturing. The Gurleyville Gristmill, dating to 1835 and standing on the Fenton River, is the only fully intact gristmill of its kind in Connecticut.

The UConn story began in 1881, when Charles and Augustus Storrs gave 170 acres and $6,000 to the state to found what was then the Storrs Agricultural College. The Mansfield Training School, a state facility on more than 1,000 acres, operated until 1993 and its former site remains part of the local landscape.

Several places in town are on the National Register of Historic Places, including the Gurleyville Historic District, the Mansfield Center Historic District and the Mansfield Hollow Historic District. If your house sits in or near one of these, ask the town what, if anything, that means for exterior changes before you start repairs.

The University of Connecticut dominates local employment. According to the town's 2024 annual financial report, as summarized by Wikipedia, UConn had 5,314 employees in Mansfield, far more than any other employer.

The age profile follows the university. In the 2000 census the median age was 22, with 44.8 percent of residents between 18 and 24. That figure is old, so treat it as a sign of the town's character and not a current number.

For a seller, the effect is a rental-heavy corner of the market around campus, plus a quieter owner-occupied market in the outer villages. A house with student tenants, an unfinished repair list or an owner who has moved away is a common situation near Storrs.

sections.h2: Which roads and buses serve Mansfield?
sections.html:
Mansfield is reached mainly by Route 195 (Storrs Road), Route 44, Route 32 and a stretch of Route 6 on its southern edge. Route 195 meets Route 44 at the intersection locals call the four corners, and Routes 44 and 32 meet at Mansfield Depot.

The Route 6 freeway section here is a leftover piece of a planned Hartford to Providence interstate that was never finished. Route 6 has an interchange with Storrs Road at the Willimantic line.

  • Windham Region Transit District runs local routes 674 and 675 and the HuskyGo campus shuttle.
  • CT Transit route 913 is an express bus between Storrs and Hartford.
  • Peter Pan Bus Lines offers limited intercity service to Hartford Union Station and Providence.
  • The Nash-Zimmer Transportation Center on Royce Circle in downtown Storrs is the local hub.

Passenger rail left the area in 1955, and the nearest historic station was in Willimantic, about nine miles south of Storrs. A reactivated rail line has been proposed but not built.

Mansfield has its own school district for the younger grades. Residents attend Mansfield Elementary School and Mansfield Middle School, and high school students attend E. O. Smith High School, which belongs to Regional School District 19.

Wikipedia notes that the former Annie E. Vinton and Dorothy C. Goodwin schools have been rebranded as campuses of Mansfield Elementary, and that Southeast Elementary was replaced. The same page says Annie E. Vinton and Dorothy C. Goodwin buildings are now used for storage. School assignments can change, so confirm the current district boundaries with the schools before you quote them to a buyer.

sections.h2: How are property taxes billed and appealed in Mansfield?
sections.html:
Mansfield taxes are based on a Grand List taken each October 1. The town's assessor page says the mill rate for the 2025 Grand List is 20.00, and that the July 2026 and January 2027 bills are based on that list.

The same page explains that every five years the assessor oversees a town-wide revaluation. The most recent one was effective October 1, 2024. After the 2024 revaluation, assessment notices were mailed in early 2025, and appeals to the Board of Assessment Appeals had to be filed by an extended deadline of April 2, 2025.

The assessor also notes that Connecticut law lets the board reduce an assessment only if the owner, an attorney or an authorized agent appears in person and is sworn in. Appeals the board declines to hear can go to Superior Court under C.G.S. 12-117a.

  • Assessor: Chandler Rose, 860-429-3311, closed Fridays.
  • Hours: Monday to Wednesday 8:00 a.m. to 5:15 p.m., Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 6:30 p.m.
  • Defective concrete and crumbling foundation information has its own page on the assessor site.

Because bills are issued per installment and follow the October 1 owner of record, ask the title company how the closing statement will split the current installment between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What does the state conveyance tax cost a Mansfield seller?
sections.html:
Connecticut charges a real estate conveyance tax on the seller, and part of it goes to the state and part to the town. Under C.G.S. 12-494, the state share on a home sale is three-quarters of one percent of the price, and the municipal share is one-quarter of one percent.

The seller, an attorney or an agent files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded with the town clerk. The state notes the tax applies when the consideration is $2,000 or more, and that the clerk cannot record the deed until the return is filed and the tax paid.

ItemRate or rule
State share, home price up to $800,0000.75%
State share, $800,000 to $2,500,000 portion1.25%
Municipal share (standard)0.25%
Filing formOP-236 with the town clerk

Certain sales are exempt, including a transfer between spouses and a principal residence sold in lieu of foreclosure. A principal residence with a pyrrhotite foundation, certified by an engineer, also has its own exemption on the first sale after certification. These are the state's descriptions, and your closing attorney will confirm what applies.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Mansfield usually face?
sections.html:
Most Mansfield sellers fall into a few groups: owners of rental houses near campus, families inheriting a house in one of the outlying villages, and homeowners with older properties needing work.

An older house in the Quiet Corner can carry deferred maintenance, and the town's historic districts add a layer to renovation planning. A listing sale means preparing the house, scheduling showings and waiting through the buyer's financing. An as-is cash sale removes those steps, and you decide whether the timing and number work for you.

  • Gather the latest tax bill and the assessor's record card for the property.
  • Confirm who holds title, especially after an inheritance.
  • Ask the town clerk's office about recording steps for your deed.
  • Ask the town about any open permits, code issues or zoning questions.

faqs.q: Is Mansfield, CT in Tolland County?
faqs.a: Yes. Mansfield is a town in Tolland County, and it belongs to the Capitol Planning Region. It was part of Windham County until 1827.

faqs.q: When are Mansfield property tax bills due?
faqs.a: Bills follow a July and January schedule. The assessor's page says the July 2026 and January 2027 bills use the 2025 Grand List with a 20.00 mill rate. Contact the Mansfield tax collector for exact due dates on your bill.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Mansfield assessment?
faqs.a: File a written appeal with the Board of Assessment Appeals by the deadline set after assessment notices go out. The board can lower an assessment only if you or your agent appears in person. Appeals it will not hear can go to Superior Court.

faqs.q: What conveyance tax does a seller pay in Connecticut?
faqs.a: On a typical home sale the seller pays 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the town, with a higher state rate on the part of a residential price above $800,000. Form OP-236 is filed when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Mansfield that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Mansfield houses sell as-is, either to a cash buyer or to a buyer who plans repairs. Gather your tax bill and title information first so the sale can move quickly.
